headline: The $0.13 API Token: Inside the Underground Relay Market for AI Access
summary: An underground market offers AI API access at a 97.8% discount, with $3,333 worth of Anthropic API credit selling for just $59. This sophisticated four-layer economy leverages stolen cards and bulk accounts.
details: $3,333 worth of official Anthropic API credit can be purchased for roughly $59, an effective rate of about $0.13 of official usage per dollar spent. This represents a staggering 97.8% discount off the list price, fueling a hidden economy.

This isn't a legitimate discount but an 'underground relay market,' a sophisticated four-layer economy that has grown around AI API tokens. Relays, also called 'transfer stations,' proxy API traffic to US-hosted AI models at deep discounts.

The massive discounts are possible because relay operators leverage stolen credit cards, bulk-registered free-trial accounts, or chargeback arbitrage. This reduces their cost per token to near zero, allowing them to sell tokens at huge discounts while still making a healthy margin.

The relay ecosystem operates with a sophisticated four-layer supply chain, as documented by security researcher Matt Lenhard. These layers range from the people sourcing raw credentials to the developers buying cheap inference.

Layer 1 consists of card and account merchants selling virtual credit cards and bulk AI provider accounts, often illicitly obtained. Layer 2, account pools, aggregates these credentials, manages authentication tokens and rate limits, and exposes a single API surface.

Layer 3, the relays or 'transfer stations,' are the consumer-facing layer, wrapping the pool's API in a clean product, handling billing, and competing on price. Layer 4 comprises end users, including individual Chinese developers, small startups, and mid-sized SaaS companies.

A significant portion of demand from end users comes from model distillation operations, where cheap relayed access to frontier models is used to train domestic alternatives. Almost all relays run on one of two open-source projects: one-api or new-api.

Both one-api and new-api are OpenAI-compatible gateways written in Go, allowing operators to deploy a panel and set up channels for various providers. Buyers simply point their existing SDK at the relay's URL, and requests are forwarded through a pool of API keys.

headline_marked: [[AI team investigates production incidents]] better than most engineers, built for SigNoz hackathon
headline: AI team investigates production incidents better than most engineers, built for SigNoz hackathon
summary: TattvaAI, an AI-powered platform, automates incident investigation by correlating observability signals and identifying root causes, drastically reducing resolution time.
details: TattvaAI, an AI-powered incident investigation platform, was developed for the SigNoz "Agents of SigNoz" Hackathon. It aims to automate the complex work of experienced Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) during production incidents.

Traditional incident response often involves hours of manual investigation to pinpoint root causes, even when the fix itself is quick. Engineers must manually connect disparate telemetry signals from various observability platforms.

TattvaAI streamlines this process by autonomously investigating incidents. It correlates evidence from multiple observability signals, identifies the most probable root cause, and provides clear explanations for its findings.

The system's architecture comprises six independent AI agents, each specializing in a different domain of observability. A central reasoning engine then combines their findings into a comprehensive investigation report.

Instead of treating SigNoz as just another dashboard, TattvaAI integrates directly, accessing telemetry via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This setup positions SigNoz as the source of truth and TattvaAI as the intelligent reasoning layer on top.

The platform was validated in a realistic microservices environment, simulating an e-commerce checkout system with an 18% error rate. Within seconds, TattvaAI identified a Redis CPU exhaustion and connection pool issue as the root cause.

TattvaAI's output includes not only the identified root cause but also the supporting evidence, confidence scores, and historical context. This ensures explainability, allowing engineers to understand the AI's conclusions and make informed decisions.
caption:
